Ka egbaseen ni

The document of/by

Husiyas

Hosea

Igpewun-a

Introduction

Ka seini ne baseen meyitenged te intagne dengan ni prupita Husiyas ne anak ni Biiri te me walu ne gatus (800) ne leg-un te ware pad neetew si Hisus. Nekeg-iling si prupita Husiyas wey si Amus ne migpanagne diye te me etew te iling ded ne timpu. Piru migpabulus-bulus mule migpanagne si Husiyas te nenakasinundul pad ne me leg-un. Te seeye ne timpu, nabaad te daruwa ka inged te Israil wey diye migwali si Husiyas te ampew ne baad ne sengekakuwa ne egngaranan din te Israil, wey sengekakuwa ne egngaranan man-e te Ipraim. Ipraim ka ngaran te amana ne impurtanti ne tribu diye te ampew ne baad. Ne ka Samarya ka iney ne siyudad. Ne ka deisek ne baad te inged te Israil, ingngaranan din te Huda. Migwali sikandin te ware pad dereeti ka Samarya te miglusud ne me kuntere dan.

This document was about the prediction of prophet Husiyas the child of Biiri long_ago at about eight hundred (800) years before Hisus was_born. Prophet Husiyas and the prophet Amus were prophesying to the people about the same time. But Husiyas continued prophesying for (more) following years. At that time, the place of Israil is divided into two and Husiyas preached there at the upper part which he sometimes called Israil, and sometimes he called Ipraim. Ipraim was the name of an important tribe in the upper part. And Samaria was the name of the capital (LIT mother) city. And the small part of the place Israil, he called_it Huda. He preached before Samarya was_destroyed when their enemies invaded (it).

Te seini ne baseen, impapitew ni Husiyas ka pegsupak te keet-etawan te Magbebaye ne Manama wey ka peg-engked dan kandin. Egpekeiling sikandan te masinupaken ne asawa rin ne si Gumir wey mig-engked kandin. Ne amana nalaggew si Husiyas tenged te pegsupak te me etew wey migsimba te me diyus-diyus, wey warad e migsalig te Magbebaye ne Manama. Piru te katammanan, iyan ded iya egdapit ka geyinawa te Manama te keet-etawan din wey egpakalibed ded man-e sikandan diye te kandin. Dakel amana ka geyinawa rin kandan, wey impanengneng din seini kayi te amana ne makalulunu ne me lalag, “Egmenuwen ku sikeykew te eg-engked, he Ipraim? Kene ku iya sikeykew egbalaharen ne egkatalu, he Israil. Kene ku sikeykew egdereetan iling te Adma wey Sibuwim. Kene egpakatuhut ka pusung ku te iling due, su dakel ka geyinawa ku keykew.” (11:8).

In this document, Husiyas showed the disobedience of the people of the Lord God (MS Manama) and their leaving of him. They were_like his disobedient spouse Gumir and left him. And Husiyas was very sad at the disobedience of the people and (who) worshiped false_gods, and no_longer trusted the Lord God. But at the end, what_persisted is the love of the Lord God to his people and they just returned again to him. His love to them is big, and he made_it_known by these very compassionate words, “How could I desert you(sg), oh Ipraim? I will_ not _abandon you(sg) to be_defeated, oh Israil. I won't destroy you(sg) like Adma and Sibuwim. My heart doesn't allow (things) like that, because my love for you(sg) is big.” (11:8).

11 [xra][xrb][xrc][xrd][xre]This is what_ the Lord God _spoke_to the (ones) from_Israil through Husiyas the child of Biiri in the time that Usiyas, Hutam, Ahas, and Isikiyas consecutively reigned in Huda and Hirubuwan the child of Huwas was the king of Israil.

Ka asawa wey me anak ni Husiyas

The spouse and children of Husiyas

2 An-anayan seini ne pegpakiglalag te Magbebaye ne Manama te me matig-Israil pinaahi ki Husiyas. Ne ingkahiyan din si Husiyas, “Hipanew ka wey pangasawa ka te malitan ne egpamelegye te lawa wey egpakaanak sikandin te me anak niyu ne egsupu kandin. Migpahunsiling sika te peg-inniyug te me matig-Israil keddi wey migsimbe e te me diyus-diyus iling te malitan ne migpamelegye te lawa.”

2 This was the first (time that) the Lord God spoke_with the (ones) from_Israil through Husiyas. And he said to Husiyas, “Go(sg) and marry(sg) a woman that sells (her) body and she can_give_birth of your(pl) children that will_be_like her. That's a metaphor of the (ones) from_Israil turning_back from me and worshiped false_gods like a woman that sells (her) body.”

3 Sikan naa ka miggipanew e si prupita Husiyas wey impangasawa rin e si Gumir ne anak ni Diblaim. Ne naberes e si Gumir wey mig-anak te lukes. 4 [xr]Ne ingkahiyan te Magbebaye ne Manama si prupita Husiyas, “Ngarani nu sikandin ki ‘Hisriil’[fn] su te kene egkaluhey eglegparan ku ka me kabuhalan ni Dihu tenged te pegpangimatey rin diye te Hisriil wey egtamanen kud ka migharian te Israil. 5 Te sika ne aldew, egpanggepuen ku ka me pane te me sundalu te Israil diye te bangalug te Hisriil.”

3 So then prophet Husiyas went and he married Gumir the child of Diblaim. And Gumir became_pregnant and bore a male (child). 4 [xr]And the Lord God said to prophet Husiyas, “Name him ‘Hisriil’[fn] because before long I will_punish the descendants of Dihu due to his killing(pl) there in Hisriil and I will_end the kingdom of Israil. 5 On that day, I will_snap the bows of the soldiers of Israil there in the valley of Hisriil.”

6 Ne nataman naberes e man-e si Gumir wey mig-anak te malitan. Ne ingkahiyan te Magbebaye ne Manama si Husiyas, “Ngarani nu sikandin ki ‘Luruhama’[fn] su kene kud e eggeyinawaan wey ke egpasayluwen naa ka me matig-Israil. 7 Piru eggeyinawaan ku mule ka me matig-Huda wey egluwasen ku sikandan, kene ne pinaahi te pane, te kampilan wey ke gira naa, te me kudde wey ke sundalu ne migmangudde, su sikeddi iya se Magbebaye ne Manama ran ka eg-uney-uney ne egluwas kandan.”

6 And then Gumir became_pregnant again and bore a female. And Husiyas was_told by the Lord God, “Name(sg) her ‘Luruhama’[fn] because I will_ no_longer _love or will_forgive the (ones) from_Israil. 7 But on_the_contrary I will_love the (ones) from_Huda and I will_save them, not by_means of the bow, of the sword or of warring, of horses or soldiers riding_horses(pl), for I will_do_it_myself as their Lord God.”

8 Te nalutas e ni Gumir si Luruhama, naberes e man-e sikandin wey mig-anak e man-e te lukes. 9 Ne migkahi ka Magbebaye ne Manama, “Ngarani nu sikandin ki Luami[fn] su kene kud e ne keet-etawan ka me matig-Israil wey kena ad ne Manama ran.”

8 When Gumir weaned Luruhama, she became_pregnant again and bore a male (child) again. 9 And the Lord God said, “Name(sg) him Luami[fn] because (ones) from_Israil are not my people anymore and I am no_longer their God.”

Ka pegpalibed te Israil diye te Manama

The returning of Israil to God

10 [xr]Piru ka keet-etawan te Israil, egpekeiling kasulug te pantad diye te dahat ne kene egkatakes, wey kene egkaseel. Ne diye te inged ne ingkahiyan sikandan te, “Kene ku sikaniyu ne keet-etawan,” egngaranan ded sikandan diye te, “Me anak te manekal ne Manama.” 11 Ne egkasabeke e man-e ka me matig-Huda wey ka me matig-Israil wey eg-alam sikandan te pangulu ran. Ne egmasulug sikandan wey egmatubung ka nasud dan.[fn] Te seeye kangkuwa ne timpu, egmabantug e ka ngaran te Hisriil.[fn]

10 [xr]But the people of Israil, are_like the numerousness of the sand at the sea that can't be measured, and can't be counted. And there at the place that they spoke_about, “You(pl) are not my people,” they will_be_named, “Children of the strong/active/living God.” 11 And the (ones) from_Huda and the (ones) from_Israil will_be_united again and they will_choose their leader. And they will_become_many and their nation will_have_abundance.[fn] On that time later, the name of Hisriil will_be_respected.[fn]

21 Purisu ngarani nu ka me suled nu ne me lukes te “Ami,”[fn] wey ngarani nu ka me atebey nu te “Ruhama.”[fn]

21 Therefore name your(sg) male brothers/cousins/mates “Ami,”[fn] and name(sg) your(sg) sisters/cousins “Ruhama.”[fn]

Ka geyinawa te Manama te keet-etawan din

The love of God of his people

31 Ne ingkahiyan a te Magbebaye ne Manama, “Hipanew kad wey geyinawei nud man-e ka asawa nu ne egpalibug-libug wey inggeyinawaan te lein ne lukes. Geyinawei nu sikandin iling te peggeyinawa te Magbebaye ne Manama te me matig-Israil minsan migsimba sikandan te me diyus-diyus, wey egkeupian ne eghalad te indampil ne behas te paras diye te me diyus-diyus.”

31 And the Lord God said to me, “Go(sg) and love again your(sg) spouse who commits_adultery and loved by other man. Love(sg) her like the loving of the Lord God to the (ones) from_Israil even_though they worship idols, and want to offer dried fruit of grapevines to false_gods.”

2 Sikan naa ka imbeli kud sikandin te kentiddad ne sapulu wey lalimma (15) ne pelata ne seleppi wey sabeka ne gatus wey lalimma ne pulu (150) ne kilu ne sibada. 3 Ne ingkahiyan ku sikandin, “Keilangan ne kene ka egsuwey keddi te egkaluhey ne timpu. Kene kad e palibug wey ke peyilabet naa te lein ne lukes. Ne minsan sikeddi, kena a degma eggulid keykew. 4 Ne iling ded degma kayi ka me matig-Israil. Egkaluhey sikandan ne eg-ugpe ne ware Hari wey ke pangulu naa, ware pegpanubad wey ke sungkaleg naa ne eglimlimuan, wey ware igsaluub ne ipud[fn] wey ke me diyus-diyus naa. 5 Piru te mewuri ne me aldew, eglibed wey eg-ikul red ka me matig-Israil te Magbebaye ne Manama ran, wey te Hari dan ne kabuhalan ni Dabid. Egparani sikandan te Magbebaye ne due pegtahud kandin, wey egpakaheram sikandan te keupiya rin.

2 That's why I bought her for the price of fifteen (15) silver coins and one hundred fifty (150) kilograms of barley. 3 And I said_to her, “It's_necessary that you(sg) don't stay_away from me for a long time. Don't(sg) commit_adultery (again) or let_other men touch_(you)_(sexually). And even me, I also won't lie_with you(sg). 4 And it's just like this for the (ones) from_Israil. They will_live for a long_time with no king or leader, no sacrificing or pillar of remembering, and no ipud[fn] or idols. 5 But in the later days, the (ones) from_Israil will_return and will_follow the Lord who is their God, and to their king a descendant of Dabid. They will_approach the Lord with respect/honor of him, and they will_experience his goodness.

The ending

1:4 Ka ngaran ne Hisriil, ngaran seini te siyudad wey te napu ne inggimatayan ni Dihu te Hari te Israil, wey te duma pad.

4:13 Iyan igpasabut kayi te Hibruwanen ne lalag ka “egpangasaween ne malitan” wey “ke ambey naa.”
